note: The other side of the line. The kernel does not judge whether an engine's claim is true, but it does insist the claim be a claim: an entry that is not a `bytes:sha256:<64 hex>` string cannot be cited, swept into an export or registered, so it is refused as a malformed policy answer by `R5e.Policy.decide/1` — the same refusal an answer outside the callback contract gets — and the admission is denied at `authorize` with `decision: "error"`. Denied rather than dropped: an engine whose report the kernel silently discarded would go on believing it had been recorded. Kernel issue #3 preserves the usable upstream decision beneath an unevaluated kernel error wrapper instead of discarding all engine evidence; malformed derived-address claims remain excluded.
